reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the first premise by showing serrated boundaries improve ductility and creep life, but it does not provide evidence for the other key premises—specifically, it does not demonstrate a thermally induced transition from serrated to straight boundaries in a single-phase alloy, nor does it show that such a transition causes embrittlement through strain localization. The proposed mechanism is largely extrapolated beyond the cited findings.
premises: Serrated grain boundaries in HEAs distribute strain evenly and increase ductility/toughness
Thermal activation can cause a transition from serrated to straight grain boundaries in single-phase HEAs
The transition is driven by local precipitate coarsening or atomic redistribution even in a single-phase alloy
Straight grain boundaries cannot arrest local strain concentrations, leading to intergranular cracking and brittle behavior
This mechanism is distinct from classical grain-boundary segregation or intermetallic precipitation
